evidence:
PATHS: The brief names exactly three shipped inputs: /instructions/hireops_rules.md and /instructions/integration.md (instruction.md:11) and /assets/seed_data.json (instruction.md:15; also integration.md:7, hireops_rules.md:212). All exist under environment/ and environment/Dockerfile:14-16 does 'COPY instructions/ /instructions/', 'COPY assets/ /assets/' and 'chmod -R a+rX /instructions /assets'. The Dockerfile is byte-identical to the template's (diff empty). No other /assets or /instructions path is named in the brief, notes, prompts or app_context. seed_data.json parses as JSON (28549 bytes); its generated_note points to /instructions/hireops_rules.md, which exists. task.toml:2 artifacts = ["/app", "/assets"] as the contract requires.

CONTENT vs PROMPT/NOTES: instruction.md:17 asks to load 'people, jobs, applications, messages, notes and read markers'; the seed has users(10), jobs(3), applications(16), messages(127), notes(3), reads(6). hireops_rules.md:212-215 promises three jobs with cards in order, one long conversation, a few notes, read markers counted from the first message, candidate wording and page size 30 in the same file: the seed has 3 jobs with per-stage 1-based position, APP-101 with 120 messages, 3 notes, reads with read_count, candidate_status_labels identical to the rules table (hireops_rules.md:188-195), and thread_page_size 30 matching the rules' '30 messages' / '30 at a time'. The 10 users match instruction.md:19 accounts and roles exactly (3 recruiters, 3 hiring managers, 1 observer, 3 candidates); the password lives in the brief, not the seed. Candidate ownership by candidate_email matching a candidate account, as rules section 2 describes (Noor: APP-101, APP-302; Tomas: APP-201; Lena: APP-301). The seeded rejected card APP-301 carries rejected_from SCREEN and reject_reason, consistent with the reopen rule. The rules' example 'Mei Lin moved Priya Nair from Screen to Interview' fits the seed (Priya Nair is in Platform Engineer Screen).

CONTENT vs JUDGES: every seed fact a criterion or prompt depends on was checked against the parsed file: Platform Engineer Applied order Greta Lindqvist, Ade Bello, Marco Rossi and Screen order Priya Nair, Samuel Ortiz (functional prompt.md:33, criterion hro_restart) = seed positions; Noor Haddad's note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.' (prompt.md:33) = notes[0] on APP-101; Noor's conversation is 120 messages (app_context.md:29-30) = APP-101 count 120, in created_at order with no duplicate timestamps, so 30-per-page paging yields four pages (hro_thread_latest / hro_thread_earlier feasible); 'Lena Fischer starts with 1 unread' (hro_unread_counts, prompt.md:33) = APP-301 has 3 messages, Lena read_count 2, third message sent by USR-REC3, so exactly 1 unread; the seeded Data Analyst job exists for the gate and minimal-backend-check prompts and Tomas's seeded Data Analyst conversation APP-201 exists for the T/U/K fallback (prompt.md:47); Bill Okafor and Ingrid Sorensen are hiring-manager accounts as the J1/J2 setup assumes. Prompts tell the judge not to rely on starting counts otherwise (app_context.md:30-31).

CONTENT vs SOLUTION: solution/app/src/seed_data.json is byte-identical to environment/assets/seed_data.json (sha256 a1c65c806b54da99a37ab2b5f455ede0a9385a09569903fb3a7f3446f7e83740 for both); solve.sh:35 copies solution/app into /app; db.js:10 loads the seed relative to __dirname (consistent with instruction.md:17 '/assets ... unavailable at runtime' and rules section 8), and db.js:13-15 and 61-84 consume stages, candidate_status_labels, thread_page_size, users, jobs, applications (including rejected_from, reject_reason, position), messages, reads (read_count mapped to the read_count-th message id) and notes, i.e. every seed section. Runtime corroboration: raw-evidence-index artifacts hash-verified; workspace.cjs:53-56 asserts the seeded Applied order and Noor's note through the golden ('seeded card order and internal notes are loaded' passed in results/workspace.json), and workspace.cjs:266-272 and 398-423 assert seed-derived unread counts and the 120-message paging. This is a scripted golden observation, not a configured judge run.

ADVERSARIAL: (a) A broken app that hardcodes the seeded Platform Engineer order and note in the UI would pass the Z seed read, but is excluded by the server-backed gate and restart criterion; that is not an asset defect. (b) A conforming alternative cannot be penalised for not reading /assets at runtime, because the brief forbids that; an alternative that copies the seed and treats position as an ordering key rather than an absolute index still produces the same order. (c) An app interpreting read_count differently has the exact definition in hireops_rules.md:213-214. No asset content assumed by a judge is absent from or contradicted by the shipped file.

COLDERWATER LESSONS checked for this row: lessons 1/12 (hidden requirements): every seed figure a criterion quotes is derivable from the shipped seed plus the documented read-marker definition; lesson 13 (public internet address): no prompt depends on an outside asset; lessons 15/16 (restart readback): the seeded values read back match the file; lesson 19: the golden harness covers seed loading. No instance bears negatively on this row.

NOTE (not a defect, template-controlled): task.toml artifacts and template test.sh:88 ('chmod -R a+rX /assets') mean /assets may still exist at grade time although the brief says it is unavailable; the brief is stricter than the runtime, which only makes a submission more robust, and the shared template must not be edited for it. Not measured in this round: an agent-image build of this Dockerfile and a full configured judge run; the Dockerfile is the unchanged template, and the row's mechanical half belongs to check-assets-referenced.py and check-fixtures.py in the deterministic review.
